Work

I design and run knowledge systems: how information is structured, governed, measured, retrieved, and kept useful as products and organizations change. These selected projects show that work across Ledger and Simple Finance.

Ledger

Knowledge Strategy, Findability & Analytics

Knowledge Management · Information Architecture · Analytics

Owned the Help Center as a knowledge product: what information exists, how it is structured, where people find it, and how it stays aligned with the product.

Reworked navigation and taxonomy around user tasks rather than internal ownership, then prioritized improvements using search behavior, traffic, case volume, dissatisfaction trends, cross-language case-to-visit ratios, and product-change data.

View Help Center  ↗

The goal was not simply more content. It was a system where the right answer surfaced at the right point in the journey, and where gaps could be traced back to structure, ownership, or product change instead of treated as isolated writing problems.

Principle: treat the Help Center as a product surface, not a filing cabinet.
Ledger

Knowledge Governance & Lifecycle

Governance · Content Operations · Migration · Taxonomy

Owned and governed internal knowledge across Business Ops, spanning logistics, operations, training, and customer-facing workflows. Led large-scale cleanup and migration work by auditing the knowledge base, assigning ownership, and triaging content into migrate, rewrite, or retire.

Built review workflows, space-wide labels, metadata standards, and weekly automation, plus a versioned knowledge-health dashboard covering several hundred pages. Managed the knowledge backlog and sprint process, and helped bridge the platform into Salesforce Knowledge with a simple feedback path for flagging inaccurate or outdated content.

The operating question is always the same: should this information still exist, is it authoritative, who owns it, and when does it need to be reviewed again? That turns a collection of pages into a maintained system rather than a growing archive.

Migration was a governance project first and a platform project second.
Ledger

AI & Retrieval Systems

AI · Retrieval · Content Standards · Measurement

Helped build Ledger’s AI knowledge experience from an early vector-database implementation through CRM-backed and customer-facing use, working on the content and retrieval layer that determines whether the system can find and return the right answer.

Developed standards for AI-ready knowledge, improved source content for retrieval reliability, tested chatbot behavior before launch, and used retrieval failures and feedback as signals for what needed to change in the knowledge underneath it.

Read the write-up  ↗

Restructuring high-volume knowledge around user language and answer-first patterns produced a measurable lift in deflection during controlled testing. The larger lesson was that AI performance depends heavily on the quality and structure of the knowledge underneath it.

Measured test: 48% deflection vs. 42% control before the pattern was expanded.
Ledger

Knowledge Capture & Operational Continuity

Knowledge Capture · Ownership · Workflow Design · Automation

Built a repeatable approach for capturing institutional knowledge before it disappears with role changes or departures. Instead of asking an SME to “document everything,” the process starts with the recurring questions other people depend on them to answer.

Those questions become reusable assets with an owner, a review path, and a place in the broader knowledge system. Built escalation routing into a dedicated knowledge-gap channel and automation for stale work so recurring gaps and follow-up items surface instead of disappearing into individual queues.

The aim is continuity: convert one-off fixes and individual expertise into knowledge that can be found, reused, validated, and governed.

Capture demand first. Then document the knowledge people actually rely on.
Ledger

Enablement & Launch Readiness

Enablement · Product Launches · Decision Support · Cross-Functional Work

Turned product changes and technical processes into usable knowledge before launch: internal one-pagers, public FAQs, troubleshooting flows, release guidance, and product education.

Built decision-support tools that helped teams apply product knowledge consistently while exposing gaps that needed to be resolved before launch.

For launches and campaigns, coordinated the same change across internal knowledge, public guidance, macros, bot responses, shipping rules, pricing and packaging, and regional restrictions. The larger job is making sure the knowledge system moves with the product, not after it.

Launch readiness is a knowledge-coordination problem, not just a documentation task.
Ledger

Learning & Development

Learning Design · E-Learning · Product Training · Knowledge Application

Designed structured learning experiences that turned complex product and operational knowledge into training people could actually use. Built payments-focused e-learning, product training for beta launches, and sales enablement for retail partners.

Focused training on decisions and real scenarios rather than information recall, connecting learning materials back to the same governed knowledge sources used across the organization.

Also helped shape an AI customer simulator for practice scenarios, using curated questions to let specialists rehearse interactions while surfacing gaps in the underlying knowledge base.

The goal was not simply to publish training. It was to create a repeatable learning system that reinforced product knowledge, exposed weak spots, and kept enablement aligned with changing products and processes.

Learning works best when training, source knowledge, and real-world decisions stay connected.
Ledger

Process & Policy Knowledge

Process Design · Policy · Operational Knowledge · Governance

Turned changing operational, legal, and product rules into repeatable workflows people could actually follow. Defined and maintained guidance for lost-asset cases, law-enforcement requests, workaround restrictions, language handling, shipping processes, and other policy-driven edge cases.

The work often started by finding contradictions or missing decisions in existing documentation, then working with the right owners to clarify the rule, document the workflow, and connect it to the places teams would actually use it.

Maintained the operational layer around those policies through one-pagers, internal guidance, escalation paths, and customer-facing updates so a policy change did not live in only one document or team.

That is a core knowledge-management problem: translating a decision into a durable process, establishing authority, and keeping every dependent surface aligned when the rule changes.

A policy is only useful when people can find it, understand it, and apply it consistently.
Ledger

Security & Trust Knowledge

Security · Trust · Information Architecture · Review Cycles

Managed security knowledge where unclear or outdated guidance can create real financial risk, including scam and phishing education, fake-app guidance, transaction and signing warnings, asset-protection information, and security-focused navigation.

Structured high-risk guidance around the decision someone needs to make next, then paired it with ownership and review paths so the information could stay useful as threats and product behavior changed.

View live example  ↗

For high-risk information, clarity and governance are inseparable. The content has to reduce confusion in the moment and remain trustworthy as threats change.

Design for the decision the user has to make next, not for the amount of information available.
Simple Finance

Product & Knowledge Foundations

Fintech · Content Strategy · Product · Research

At Simple Finance, product content, help documentation, persona work, and feature development were closely tied to user interviews, behavioral data, and sprint planning.

That is where the operating model behind my later knowledge work took shape: information should have an owner, a lifespan, a measurable purpose, and a direct connection to the product experience.

The standard carried forward: content decisions should be justified by user outcomes, not just by accuracy or style.

Foundation: content is part of the product system, not a separate layer added afterward.
The Through-Line

Knowledge management is the system underneath the visible content: what exists, who owns it, how people find it, how it stays current, and how tools such as AI retrieve it. Writing is one part of that system, not the job itself.

The work spans information architecture, governance, analytics, enablement, AI retrieval, and product operations because those disciplines meet in the same place: reliable knowledge.
